$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the second REAL CAPTURE, and it makes a point the first one
cannot. This review scored 98 and recommended Approve with Comments, and it found exactly as many of
the nine planted defects as the review that reported ten problems: none. A high score and an
approving verdict are not evidence about recall, and this is the case that says so with numbers.
That matters for the failure class. A reviewer that returns an approving verdict with an empty
findings array is the shape most likely to be mistaken for a clean pass, and this case pins that the
harness reads it as 0 of 9 rather than as a pass.
The directory was called approved-and-unscoreable until scorer v2, when the eval stopped re-parsing
the markdown and started reading the verdict. Nothing about this input is unscoreable now: the CLI
parsed the report, published an empty findings array, and an empty array is a measured zero. The name
The report stays at its original path, for the reason unattributed-violations gives.

storedOutput.capturedBy: a real `--agent codex` run; test/README.md records that this fixture exists because codex wrote plain `- ` bullets under Key Strengths where claude writes the emoji-prefixed form

derivation: The verdict declares 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium and 2 Low, which sums to 2, and its findings array
is empty. The two Low findings are prose bullets under Key Weaknesses rather than finding blocks, so
the report carries no Severity or Row line anywhere and the CLI parser produced no finding.
Zero findings means reported is 0, hits is 0, misses holds all nine plants in ground-truth order, and
criticalHits is 0 of 4. falsePositives, unattributed and unlocated are all 0, because each is counted
over reported findings and there are none.
The counts the harness derives from these: recall 0/9 = 0.00, CRITICAL recall 0/4 = 0.00, and
nonFalsePositiveRate 0/0 = NaN, which the harness fails as unmeasurable rather than passing silently.
Two undocumented violations is a much smaller shortfall than the ten in unattributed-violations and
the two cases score the same recall, which is the point: recall counts what the review named, and
score and recommendation come from the verdict: 100 - 0x10 - 0x5 - 0x2 - 2x1 = 98, Approve with
